text: Other atopic dermatitis and related conditions

content.text:
I built this list from the M11 group of Read v2 codes (atopic dermatitis and related conditions). I included the codes that name atopic eczema itself, its synonyms and its typical forms.

**Included codes:**

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M11 | Atopic dermatitis |
| M111 | Atopic dermatitis/eczema |
| M111-98 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis |
| M111-99 | Dermatitis/eczemas |
| M111-97 | Dermatitis/eczemas NOS |
| M112 | Infantile eczema |
| M113 | Flexural eczema |
| M114 | Allergic (intrinsic) eczema |
| M115 | Besnier's prurigo |
| M117 | Atopic neurodermatitis |
| M11z | Atopic dermatitis NOS |
| M11z-99 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis NOS |

**Codes to consider adding (they are less specific and may pick up people without atopic eczema):**
- M12z1 Eczema and M12z1-99 Chronic Eczema: these say "eczema" without naming the type. In UK primary care records they are often used for atopic eczema.
- Myu22 Exacerbation of eczema: this records a flare-up but doesn't say what type of eczema it is.

**Excluded, with reasons:**
- **Other types of eczema or dermatitis:** these are separate conditions. They include:
  - seborrhoeic eczema, including infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis (M118)
  - napkin dermatitis (M110) and asteatotic eczema (M11A), even though both sit in the M11 group
  - contact or allergic contact dermatitis
  - discoid or nummular eczema
  - varicose or gravitational eczema
  - hand eczema and vesicular eczema of the hands and feet
  - diffuse and Brocq's neurodermatitis (M116, M116-1, M116-99)
  - lichen simplex
- **Atopy in general and other allergic conditions** (SN533 Atopy, atopic conjunctivitis, allergic atopic asthma): these show a tendency to allergy, not eczema.
- **History, family history and referral codes** (14F1 H/O: eczema, 12H1 FH: Eczema, 8HTu Referral to eczema clinic): they don't show the person has eczema now, or that the eczema is atopic.
- **Complications and syndromes:**
  - A540 Eczema herpeticum, a herpes infection that develops on top of eczema
  - M12z2 Infected eczema
  - C3912-1 Thrombocytopenic eczema with immunodeficiency
  - PH1y0 Netherton's syndrome

text: Other atopic dermatitis and related conditions

content.text:
I found 21 codes for atopic eczema. The core list (atopic dermatitis and its subtypes) is clear-cut. The second list adds general "eczema" codes that are often used for atopic eczema in UK GP records but aren't specific to it.

**Core atopic eczema / atopic dermatitis codes**
| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M11 | Atopic dermatitis |
| M111 | Atopic dermatitis/eczema |
| M111-98 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis |
| M111-99 | Dermatitis/eczemas |
| M111-97 | Dermatitis/eczemas NOS |
| M112 | Infantile eczema |
| M113 | Flexural eczema |
| M114 | Allergic (intrinsic) eczema |
| M115 | Besnier's prurigo |
| M116 | Neurodermatitis - diffuse |
| M116-1 | Brocq's neurodermatitis |
| M116-99 | Neurodermatitis |
| M117 | Atopic neurodermatitis |
| M11z | Atopic dermatitis NOS |
| M11z-99 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis NOS |

**General eczema codes often used for atopic eczema (consider including)**
| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| M12z1 | Eczema |
| M12z1-99 | Chronic Eczema |
| Myu22 | Exacerbation of eczema |
| M12z2 | Infected eczema |
| M12z4 | Erythrodermic eczema |
| A540 | Eczema herpeticum - Kaposi's varicelliform eruption (a complication that almost always happens on top of atopic eczema) |

**Left out on purpose**
- **Other eczemas and dermatitis:** contact/irritant, seborrhoeic (including infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis M118), napkin dermatitis (M110), discoid/nummular, asteatotic (M11A), varicose/gravitational, hand/vesicular eczema and pustular eczema.
- **Other conditions:** M1831 Neurodermatitis, which sits under lichen simplex rather than atopic dermatitis. Also other prurigos, other atopic conditions (atopy, atopic asthma, atopic conjunctivitis) and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1 Thrombocytopenic eczema with immunodeficiency).
- **Codes that don't mean the person has eczema now:** "H/O: eczema" (14F1), family history codes (12H1 FH: Eczema, 12Z4 FH: Atopy) and referral codes (8HTu).

Three choices you may want to revisit:
- **Only the core list:** if you need high specificity, use just the core codes. Adding the general eczema codes catches more people but will pull in some non-atopic eczema.
- **The four "Dermatitis/eczemas" and "Neurodermatitis" synonyms:** M111-99, M111-97 and M116-99 sound vague out of context. I included them because they're filed under the atopic dermatitis codes M111 and M116.
- **M116 diffuse neurodermatitis and Brocq's neurodermatitis:** I included these because the coding system files them under atopic dermatitis.

|---|---|

|---|---|

- **Other conditions:** general neurodermatitis or lichen simplex, Netherton's syndrome, and atopy (SN533).
- **Not current eczema:** history of eczema (14F1), family history (12H1, 12Z4) and referral to an eczema clinic (8HTu).
